intended_object: This is an auxiliary limit cone. It takes the profinite limit cone (Profinite.limitCone) of the cofiltered diagram of finite sets that comes from the chosen Ind-presentation of a dual ind-object Q. The library uses it as a step toward the functor `indDualRealization : (Ind FintypeCat.Skeletonᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Profinite`. This is inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it.
explanation:
The body just applies Mathlib's `Profinite.limitCone` to one diagram. That diagram comes from `Q.unop.presentation`, an Ind-presentation chosen noncomputably for Q. It is pushed into finite sets and then into profinite spaces. The result is bundled data used to define the object part (`.pt`) and the morphism part of `indDualRealization`.

As a construction it is correct: it is the standard limit cone in Profinite of a cofiltered system of finite discrete spaces. But it is not a notion that appears in its own right in the literature. It is an implementation step in building the realization functor from pro-finite sets to profinite spaces, and it depends on a chosen presentation. So it is best classed as a technical device rather than a mathematical object. There is nothing incorrect in it, and it is not too narrow.
